cover.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: full-width cover illustration for Week in Hazel, 3:2 landscape, no typography
Primary request: Create a completely new editorial woodcut/linocut illustration for a retrospective issue about Backpack II: a small fictional traveler made of simple carved shapes crosses a landscape built from interlocking programming-language syntax tiles. The traveler carries a translucent, almost empty backpack whose only contents are missing delimiter shards: a closing parenthesis, the word end, the word in, and a small => arrow. The bag should visually convey that it is derived from what the surrounding syntax lacks, not a permanent inventory.
Style reference: use the supplied prior cover only for the publication's restrained handmade print language, warm ivory paper, forest-black ink, moss green, vermilion, and muted yellow. Do not reuse its composition, characters, objects, tree motif, or narrative.
Composition: wide scene with the traveler slightly left of center and the tiled path sweeping toward the right; enough calm negative space for cropping. Complete illustration fills the frame; no border, frame, mat, magazine title, caption, labels, speech balloons, or readable text beyond the four deliberate delimiter symbols in the bag.
Quality: crisp at print size, sparse fine grain, lively irregular edges, not heavy dark woodgrain.
cover.summary: A new woodcut traveler crosses syntax tiles carrying only missing delimiter shards; the prior cover supplied visual language only.
cover.known_limits: The backpack symbols are conceptual and are not a Hazel screenshot or syntax specification.

comic.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: three-panel horizontal fictional comic strip for Week in Hazel, 3:1 aspect ratio
Primary request: Create a completely new wordless comic about an unused-variable warning that arrives, is immediately recalled, and leaves a faint orange outline behind. Panel 1: at a tiny railway platform made of syntax tiles, an earnest orange warning clerk steps off a train carrying a clipboard while a small question-mark creature watches. Panel 2: the clerk begins carefully outlining an apparently unused blue variable tile, but a large empty hole in the surrounding program opens like a doorway, suggesting the variable could still be used there. Panel 3: the return train departs with the clerk aboard; the question-mark creature and variable tile remain, looking at the unresolved hole. Gentle dry humor, no real people.
Style reference: use the supplied comic only for the publication's restrained carved-print visual language, warm ivory paper, forest-black, moss green, vermilion/orange, muted yellow, uneven ink and sparse grain. Do not reuse its characters, office composition, props, or narrative.
Hard constraints: three clearly separated panels; no speech balloons; no captions; no letters, words, numbers, logos, watermarks, or other readable text anywhere. Complete unframed artwork; no heavy woodgrain.
comic.summary: A wordless three-panel warning clerk arrives, outlines a variable near a hole, and departs.

unused_variable_stamp.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: publishable stamp facsimile of an authentic Hazel screenshot
Input images: Image 1 is the content reference and must determine the entire crop, code, labels, values, and geometry. Image 2 is style reference only.
Primary request: Reproduce Image 1 as faithfully as a meticulous stamp-maker reproducing a software screenshot. Preserve every visible code character, punctuation mark, variable name, number, line break, selection, warning outline, breadcrumb, and UI relationship from Image 1. Keep its tall aspect ratio and complete crop.
Style: Image 2 supplies only the restrained printed quality: slightly irregular ink edges, light pigment variation, warm pale paper, sparse fine grain, limited moss green and vermilion/orange. Favor this lightly stamped Cards exemplar.
Hard constraints: text and values remain crisp and readable; do not invent, omit, reorder, or correct any source text; do not import cards or subjects from Image 2; no added border, mat, corner marks, heavy woodgrain, dark bands, thick carved outlines, or decoration.
unused_variable_stamp.fidelity: The major labels, values, line structure and orange/red distinction were visually checked. The original PNG remains the exact syntax/UI evidence.

scrollbar_stamp.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: publishable stamp facsimile of an authentic Hazel screenshot
Input images: Image 1 is the content reference and must determine the entire crop, source code, labels, controls, scrollbar, icons, and geometry. Image 2 is style reference only.
Primary request: Reproduce Image 1 faithfully as a restrained printed stamp. Preserve every visible character and line of the staged EmojiPaint MVU type declarations, the scratch/scratchpad 2 breadcrumb, the top bar, the right-side scrollbar extending below the bar, both sidebar icons, and the complete crop. The scrollbar-under-top-bar relationship is the technical point and must remain unambiguous.
Style: Image 2 supplies only slight irregular ink edges, light pigment variation, warm pale paper, sparse fine grain, moss green, muted gold and restrained vermilion.
Hard constraints: keep text crisp and readable; no invented or changed code; no added border, mat, corner marks, cards, decorations, heavy woodgrain, dark bands, or thick outlines; keep the wide aspect ratio.
scrollbar_stamp.fidelity: The four visible type declarations and scrollbar/top-bar relationship were visually checked. The original PNG remains the exact UI evidence.
